text.p: The Supreme Court of New South Wales on Monday adjourned until Tuesday a hearing to approve the merger between Advance Bank Australia Ltd and St George Bank Ltd.

Justice Kim Santow called for more submissions from Advance Bank relating to the drafting of the legal documentation of the scheme as well as a response by Advance to the submissions from company watchdog, the Australian Securities Commission (ASC).
The ASC said it would respond to Advance's submissions after the bank had completed them.
An Advance spokesman said the merger timing was still on track.

The ASC has said it would not oppose the scheme mechanism, which allows Advance to vote proxies obtained from its December 23, 1996, shareholder meeting at the second shareholder meeting on January 13 to alter its articles of association.
Advance decided to adopt this deemed proxy procedure to stop the possibility of a single shareholder frustrating the deal at the later meetings.
National Australia Bank Ltd has a three percent stake in Advance and 6.8 percent of St George. NAB, which is seen as interested in buying regional banks, has not said whether it opposes the merger.
Shareholders at last month's Advance meeting voted overwhelmingly to approve the merger.
Asked by Reuters whether Advance was surprised that the court hearing would run into a second day, the Advance spokesman replied: "We believed there was every chance that would be the case."
